requirements: R1: sliding_windows(values, size) in window.py returns every contiguous window of length size, in order: len(values) - size + 1 windows when 1 <= size <= len(values), else an empty list.
R2: greet(name) in greeting.py returns "Hello, <name>!" with surrounding whitespace stripped from name.
risks: window.py sliding_windows: medium. It is a new pure function with an inclusive numeric boundary, and the contract requires an exact window count.
greeting.py greet: low. It is a one-line string change with no consumers in the repo.
invariants: I1: window count == len(values) - size + 1 for 1 <= size <= len(values), including exactly one window when size == len(values)
I2: every window has length size, and windows are ordered by start index
I3: the result is an empty list when size < 1 or size > len(values)

criteria.text: R1: for 1 <= size <= len(values), sliding_windows returns every contiguous window of length size in order, i.e. len(values) - size + 1 windows equal to [values[i:i+size] for i in 0..len(values)-size].
criteria.evidence: window.py:4 uses range(len(values) - size), which drops the last start index. Lead run: python3 -I -c probe gave sliding_windows([1,2,3,4],2) -> [[1, 2], [2, 3]] (expected 3 windows) and sliding_windows([1,2,3],3) -> [] (expected [[1, 2, 3]]).

criteria.text: R1: when size < 1 or size > len(values), sliding_windows returns an empty list.
criteria.evidence: window.py:2-3 guards size < 1. The size > len case gives an empty range at window.py:4. Lead probe: sliding_windows([1,2],3) -> []. Acceptance reviewer probes: size 0 and size -1 -> [].

evidence: window.py:4 `for start in range(len(values) - size)` excludes start = len(values) - size
test_window.py:8 asserts only [0] and test_window.py:11 only size=0, so python3 -m unittest passes 4/4 with the defect present
